subject: maths
question: Two tangents, PA and PB, are drawn from an external point P to a circle with a radius of 10 cm. If the angle between the two tangents is 90 degrees, what is the distance from point P to the center of the circle?
solution:
**Given:**

Radius of circle r = 10 cm

PA and PB are tangents from external point P

Angle APB = 90°

**Formula used:**

Angle between tangents = 180° − angle AOB

In right triangle: OP² = OA² + AP²

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/32e0f2606fa348dac1d4943d02601c0b351a3606f9466afc3e5b6a4f8ebd4730.png] 

**Calculation:**

Angle APB = 90°

⇒ 180° − angle AOB = 90°

⇒ angle AOB = 90°

OA ⟂ AP

In ΔOAP

OA = 10

Angle OAP = 45° (bisected)

⇒ tan 45° = AP / OA

⇒ 1 = AP / 10

⇒ AP = 10

Now in right ΔOAP

⇒ OP² = OA² + AP²

⇒ OP² = 10² + 10²

⇒ OP² = 200

⇒ OP = √200 = 10√2

**∴ The distance from point P to the center is 10√2 cm.**
